title: Integral as a probability-weighted sum on a finite probability space
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite probability space, and let $p(\omega)$ denote the probability mass it assigns to each point $\omega \in \Omega$. Then for every function $f \colon \Omega \to \bbr$,
\[
  \int_\Omega f(\omega)\,d\omega \;=\; \sum_{\omega \in \Omega} p(\omega)\, f(\omega),
\]
so that the expectation of $f$ under the canonical probability measure equals the finite $p$-weighted sum of its values.
hypotheses_covered: Ω is a finite probability space
f is a real-valued function on Ω
p(ω) is the probability mass of ω
